Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

in exchange for preposition

also in return for, for (in return), for (a price), swap for, trade for

classical

Ter. Ph. 336: prō maleficiō … beneficium … reddere
Tac. Ann. 4.18: prō grātiā odium redditur

prō + abl.

preposition with the ablative

in exchange for, in return for

What is given or paid back for something: prō meritō, as one deserves.

Other words

  • cāsus ablātīvus — for (a price)

    construction: the price in the ablative, with verbs of buying, selling and costing · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 191: minīs vīgintī tū illam ēmistī; Mt. 10.29: duo passerēs asse vēneunt

    “For how much?” is the genitive of value, quantī?. With mūtāre the thing exchanged stands in the ablative (see trade).

  • contrā — in return

    adverb · also used · classical · Catull. 13.9: sed contrā accipiēs merōs amōrēs

Examples

  • Alere nōlunt hominem edācem; et sapiunt, meā quidem sententiā, prō maleficiō sī beneficium summum nōlunt reddere.

    They don’t want to feed a greedy man; and they are wise, in my opinion, if they don’t want to return the greatest kindness for a wrong.Ter. Ph. 335–336

  • Nōn potest satis prō meritō ab illō tibi referrī grātia.

    He can never thank you enough for what you have done.Ter. Ph. 337

  • Minīs vīgintī tū illam ēmistī; quae rēs tibi vertat male. Argentī tantum dabitur.

    You bought her for twenty minae (and may it bring you bad luck): that much money will be paid.Ter. Ad. 191–192

  • Nōnne duo passerēs asse vēneunt?

    Are not two sparrows sold for a penny?Mt. 10.29

  • nam beneficia eō ūsque laeta sunt dum videntur exolvī posse: ubi multum antevēnēre prō grātiā odium redditur

    favours are welcome only as long as it seems they can be repaid; once they far outrun that, hatred is returned for gratitudeTac. Ann. 4.18

  • sed contrā accipiēs merōs amōrēs

    but in return you will get pure loveCatull. 13.9

See also trade, price, buy, for.
